task: Update a mixture after adding items
formula: A:B = a:b ⇒ A=ak, B=bk; new total = old total + g.
condition: An added share is measured against the final total.

narration: The blue block is the original mixture. Adding green counters creates the amber block and also increases the denominator. The new green probability is g divided by forty-eight plus g. A stated fraction of the final mixture is not a fraction of the original group.

formula: P(A and B)=P(A)P(B); add mutually exclusive path products.
condition: Use unchanged branch probabilities only for independent events.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A weighted two-toss tree shows that equally named paths can have different probabilities."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="86" r="4" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="86" x2="160" y2="35" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="86" x2="160" y2="135" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="110" y="39" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">3/5</text><text x="110" y="145" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">2/5</text><text x="182" y="42" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">H</text><text x="182" y="144" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">T</text><line x1="198" y1="35" x2="315" y2="13" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="198" y1="35" x2="315" y2="57" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="198" y1="135" x2="315" y2="113" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="198" y1="135" x2="315" y2="157" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="381" y="25" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">HH: 9/25</text><text x="381" y="67" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">HT: 6/25</text><text x="381" y="122" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">TH: 6/25</text><text x="381" y="167" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">TT: 4/25</text></svg>
narration: Follow one complete path and multiply its branch probabilities. To find an event with several separate paths, add those path products. The tree uses a biased coin, so independence does not make heads and tails equally likely or give all result categories equal probabilities.

formula: Probability follows physical faces or sector angles.
condition: Distinct labels need not have equal probabilities.

narration: Each square is one equally likely physical face. Count three faces labelled two, even though two is only one of the distinct labels. The probability is therefore three sixths. For a spinner, compare sector angles rather than simply counting different colour names.

formula: Estimated P(E)=successes/trials; expected count=n × P(E).
condition: An expectation assumes comparable conditions; it is not a guarantee.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Past successes give an estimated probability which is multiplied by future trial count."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="35" y="37" width="170" height="65" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="275" y="37" width="170" height="65" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="120" y="63" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">42 / 70</text><text x="120" y="90" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">past trials</text><line x1="215" y1="69" x2="265" y2="69" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="265.0,69.0 257.6,72.1 257.6,65.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="360" y="63" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">0.6 × 150</text><text x="360" y="90" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">future trials</text><text x="240" y="151" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Estimate → expected count 90</text></svg>
narration: Use the fraction of past trials that succeeded as an estimate of probability. Multiply that estimate by the number of comparable future trials. Here forty-two successes out of seventy suggest ninety in one hundred and fifty. An expected count does not guarantee the actual result.

formula:
n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B)
n(A∪B∪C)=n(A)+n(B)+n(C)−n(A∩B)−n(A∩C)−n(B∩C)+n(A∩B∩C)
condition: Pair intersections include the triple overlap.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Three intersecting circles show the triple counted three times in the single-set totals."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="208" cy="74" r="55" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="272" cy="74" r="55" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="240" cy="119" r="43" fill="none" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="161" y="40" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">A</text><text x="320" y="40" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">B</text><text x="290" y="166" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">C</text><text x="240" y="89" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">×3</text><text x="63" y="78" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Add</text><text x="63" y="108" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">singles</text><text x="409" y="78" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">− pairs</text><text x="409" y="108" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">+ triple</text></svg>
narration: Start with the single-set totals, subtract every pair intersection, and add back the triple intersection once. Pair intersections already contain the triple region. Fill the centre first when numbers are given, then work outward so each person or outcome occupies exactly one region.

formula: Or = union; and = intersection; exactly one = single-set-only regions.
condition: “At least two” includes the triple region in a three-set diagram.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two overlapping circles distinguish the overlap from the regions belonging to exactly one set."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="160" cy="80" r="55" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="225" cy="80" r="55" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M192.5 35.6 A55 55 0 0 1 192.5 124.4 A55 55 0 0 1 192.5 35.6" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="141" y="86" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">A</text><text x="244" y="86" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">B</text><text x="193" y="86" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">∩</text><text x="240" y="159" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">AND: overlap   OR: either circle</text><text x="365" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Exactly one:</text><text x="365" y="91" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">leave out</text><text x="365" y="122" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">the overlap</text></svg>
narration: And selects the shared overlap. Or includes every region in either circle, including the overlap. Exactly one selects the two outer parts and leaves the overlap out. With three sets, at least two also includes the central region where all three sets meet.

formula: P(A then B)=P(A) × P(B given A).
condition: After removing one counter, update both counts and the total.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A two-draw tree from four red and three blue counters changes its second-draw probabilities after the first draw."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="90" r="4" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="90" x2="165" y2="42" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="90" x2="165" y2="138" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="104" y="43" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">4/7 R</text><text x="104" y="150" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">3/7 B</text><line x1="165" y1="42" x2="320" y2="22" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="165" y1="42" x2="320" y2="67" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="165" y1="138" x2="320" y2="114" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="165" y1="138" x2="320" y2="160" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="379" y="27" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">3/6 R</text><text x="379" y="73" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">3/6 B</text><text x="379" y="119" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">4/6 R</text><text x="379" y="168" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">2/6 B</text></svg>
narration: The first draw has seven counters available. Without replacement, every second branch has only six. If red was removed, three red remain; if blue was removed, four red remain. Multiply along each required path using these updated conditional probabilities, then add separate paths if needed.

formula: Multiply every term by the LCM of the denominators.
condition: Denominators must be non-zero; multiply the right-hand side too.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Multiplying every term of x over two plus y over three equals five by six clears both fractions."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="26" y="35" width="428" height="55" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="70" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">x/2 + y/3 = 5</text><line x1="240" y1="95" x2="240" y2="120" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="240.0,120.0 236.9,112.6 243.1,112.6" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="119" y="117" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">× 6</text><text x="240" y="157" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">3x + 2y = 30</text></svg>
narration: Choose the least common multiple of the denominators. Multiply every term on both sides by it, not just the terms written as fractions. Here multiplying by six produces three x plus two y equals thirty, an equivalent equation ready for elimination or substitution.

formula: Use equivalent operations; the answer must satisfy both equations.
condition: Choose matching coefficients for elimination, or an isolated variable for substitution.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Subtracting two equations cancels their matching y terms, then substitution finds y."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="36" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">2x + y = 18</text><text x="150" y="78" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">x + y = 11</text><line x1="42" y1="93" x2="255" y2="93" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="130" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x = 7</text><text x="345" y="63" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">subtract</text><line x1="285" y1="95" x2="285" y2="120" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="285.0,120.0 281.9,112.6 288.1,112.6" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="366" y="149" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">y = 11 − 7 = 4</text></svg>
narration: Subtract the second equation from the first so the equal y terms cancel. This leaves x equal to seven. Put that value into either original equation to get y equal to four. Finally substitute both values into both original equations to confirm the common solution.

formula: Total = quantity₁ × rate₁ + quantity₂ × rate₂.
condition: Define unknown rates and keep their units consistent.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two blocks separate hours at one unknown rate from hours at a second unknown rate."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="27" y="37" width="170" height="68" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="283" y="37" width="170" height="68" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="112" y="66" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">6 hours × r</text><text x="112" y="94" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">first rate</text><text x="368" y="66" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">2 hours × s</text><text x="368" y="94" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">second rate</text><text x="240" y="83" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">+</text><text x="240" y="154" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">6r + 2s = total pay</text></svg>
narration: The blocks represent two contributions to total pay. Hours are known quantities multiplying unknown hourly rates. Add the two contributions to make one equation for the total. A second situation gives another equation. Define your unknowns before deciding which numbers are coefficients.

task: Separate fixed cost and daily rate
formula: C=F+nd; two different n-values identify F and d.
condition: The fixed charge occurs once, not once per day.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A single fixed-charge block is followed by three equal daily-charge blocks."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="25" y="36" width="105" height="68" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="78" y="64" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">F</text><text x="78" y="93" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">once</text><text x="153" y="79" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">+</text><rect x="180" y="36" width="77" height="68" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="218" y="78" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">d</text><rect x="270" y="36" width="77" height="68" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="308" y="78" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">d</text><rect x="360" y="36" width="77" height="68" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="398" y="78" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">d</text><text x="240" y="153" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">C = F + 3d</text><text x="315" y="27" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">3 daily charges</text></svg>
narration: Read the amber block as a charge paid once, and each green block as one day at rate d. A longer hire adds daily blocks but not another fixed charge. Subtract costs for two different durations to find the daily rate, then recover the fixed charge.

formula: k years ago: x−k; changed fraction: (n+a)/(d+b).
condition: Require d+b≠0. Twice a past age is 2(x−k).
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A timeline distinguishes a past age from a current age; a changed fraction groups each entire numerator and denominator."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="53" x2="430" y2="53" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="430.0,53.0 422.6,56.1 422.6,49.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="90" y="30" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">x − k</text><text x="384" y="30" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">x now</text><text x="240" y="91" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">k years later</text><rect x="70" y="113" width="340" height="47" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="145" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Changed fraction: (n+a)/(d+b)</text></svg>
narration: Move backward along the timeline by subtracting the same number of years from each person. If a statement doubles a past age, double the whole bracket. For changed fractions, group the full new numerator and denominator, and check that the new denominator cannot be zero.

formula: P=2(L+W); halving W gives P_folded=2L+W.
condition: A fold changes one dimension; it need not halve the perimeter.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A rectangle folded across its width keeps its length but halves the width."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="45" y="40" width="170" height="95" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="87.5" x2="215" y2="87.5" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="130" y="30" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">L</text><text x="24" y="96" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">W</text><line x1="230" y1="88" x2="282" y2="88" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="282.0,88.0 274.6,91.1 274.6,84.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="300" y="40" width="150" height="47.5" rx="0" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="375" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">L</text><text x="374" y="128" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">W/2</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">2L + 2W → 2L + W</text></svg>
narration: The dashed fold line halves the width while preserving the length. Trace the new outside boundary: it has two lengths and two half-widths. That gives two L plus W. Combine this with the original perimeter equation to find the two original dimensions.

formula: Crossing: 1 solution; distinct parallel: 0; coincident: infinitely many.
condition: A simultaneous solution is a point on both lines.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Three mini diagrams compare crossing, parallel and coincident lines."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="20" y="20" width="130" height="105" rx="7" fill="#fff" stroke="#d8e3e8" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="105" x2="130" y2="40" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="40" y1="40" x2="130" y2="105" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="85" cy="72.5" r="4" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="85" y="155" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">One pair</text><rect x="175" y="20" width="130" height="105" rx="7" fill="#fff" stroke="#d8e3e8" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="190" y1="85" x2="280" y2="30" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="200" y1="113" x2="290" y2="58" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><text x="240" y="155" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">No pair</text><rect x="330" y="20" width="130" height="105" rx="7" fill="#fff" stroke="#d8e3e8" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="350" y1="105" x2="440" y2="40" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="5"/><line x1="350" y1="105" x2="440" y2="40" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="395" y="155" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Infinite</text></svg>
narration: Look for points shared by both lines. Crossing lines share one point. Distinct parallel lines never meet, while coincident lines share every point. During elimination, a false statement means no solution; an identity can indicate that the two equations describe the same line.

task: Find a direct or multi-leg distance
formula: AB=√[(x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²]; via C: AC+CB.
condition: Use the distance formula for each straight leg of a route.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Horizontal and vertical changes form a right triangle; the direct route is its hypotenuse."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="75,133 385,133 385,35" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="75" y1="133" x2="385" y2="35" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><text x="58" y="156" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">A</text><text x="409" y="36" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">B</text><text x="409" y="153" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">C</text><text x="228" y="163" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">Δx</text><text x="420" y="91" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">Δy</text><text x="220" y="64" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">direct AB</text><path d="M369 133 L369 117 L385 117" fill="none" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/></svg>
narration: The blue legs are changes in coordinates. The green diagonal is the direct distance, found by Pythagoras. A route through another point means adding its separate leg lengths. In the example with legs six and eight, the direct distance is ten but the two-leg route is fourteen.

task: Find a midpoint or missing endpoint
condition: Apply the missing-endpoint rule separately to each coordinate.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="The midpoint splits a segment into two equal displacements, allowing a missing endpoint to be reconstructed."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="55" y1="110" x2="425" y2="40" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="55" cy="110" r="6" fill="#3175ba" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="240" cy="75" r="6" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="425" cy="40" r="6" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="65" y="147" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">A(−3,2)</text><text x="237" y="52" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">M(1,5)</text><text x="405" y="83" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">B(5,8)</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">A → M = M → B</text></svg>
narration: The midpoint lies halfway between the endpoints in both coordinates. Average x values and y values separately to find it. To work backward, double each midpoint coordinate and subtract the matching known endpoint coordinate. Equal moves from A to M and M to B confirm the result.

task: Find a slope and its exceptions
formula: m=(y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁); horizontal m=0; vertical undefined.
condition: Require x₂≠x₁ for the fraction; keep subtraction order consistent.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A slope triangle separates horizontal run from vertical rise."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="38" y1="138" x2="444" y2="138" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="444.0,138.0 436.6,141.1 436.6,134.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="100" y1="158" x2="100" y2="22" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="100.0,22.0 103.1,29.4 96.9,29.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="452" y="146" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">x</text><text x="84" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">y</text><line x1="115" y1="123" x2="370" y2="38" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="150" y1="111" x2="340" y2="111" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="340" y1="111" x2="340" y2="48" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="3"/><text x="239" y="132" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">run</text><text x="383" y="86" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">rise</text><text x="255" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">m = rise / run</text></svg>
narration: Choose one direction between the points and keep it for both coordinate differences. Divide the vertical change by the horizontal change. A horizontal line has zero rise. A vertical line has zero run, so its gradient is undefined because division by zero is not allowed.

task: Build a line from a point and slope
formula: y−y₁=m(x−x₁).
condition: Keep coordinates grouped: subtracting a negative becomes addition.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A known point anchors a slope triangle whose rise equals slope times run."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="38" y1="138" x2="444" y2="138" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="444.0,138.0 436.6,141.1 436.6,134.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="100" y1="158" x2="100" y2="22" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="100.0,22.0 103.1,29.4 96.9,29.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="452" y="146" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">x</text><text x="84" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">y</text><line x1="70" y1="149" x2="400" y2="39" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="220" cy="99" r="7" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="245" y="76" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">(x₁, y₁)</text><line x1="220" y1="99" x2="340" y2="99" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="340" y1="99" x2="340" y2="59" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="280" y="124" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">x − x₁</text><text x="395" y="99" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">y − y₁</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">rise = m × run</text></svg>
narration: The amber point is a known point on the line. From it, the horizontal change is x minus x one and the vertical change is y minus y one. The gradient connects these changes. Substitute the known point and slope before expanding or rearranging the equation.

formula: ax+by+c=0 ⇒ y=−(a/b)x−c/b; m=−a/b.
condition: Require b≠0. Isolate y before reading off coefficients.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="An equation in general form is rearranged to y equals m x plus c, exposing the slope and intercept."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="25" y="20" width="430" height="46" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="51" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">3x + 2y − 8 = 0</text><line x1="240" y1="72" x2="240" y2="94" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="240.0,94.0 236.9,86.6 243.1,86.6" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="128" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="29" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">y = −(3/2)x + 4</text><text x="142" y="168" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">slope −3/2</text><text x="350" y="168" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">intercept 4</text></svg>
narration: Start by making y the subject. Only then read the multiplier of x as the gradient and the constant as the y-intercept. In the example, dividing every term by two gives negative three halves for the slope and four for the intercept.

formula: Parallel: m₁=m₂; perpendicular finite slopes: m₁m₂=−1. Horizontal y=k has m=0; vertical x=k is undefined.
condition: A horizontal–vertical pair is perpendicular; do not multiply undefined slopes.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Parallel lines share a slope; a separate pair meets at a right angle."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="35" y1="120" x2="195" y2="40" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="35" y1="83" x2="165" y2="18" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><text x="117" y="164" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">m₁ = m₂</text><line x1="290" y1="119" x2="424" y2="52" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="327" y1="25" x2="382" y2="135" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><text x="418" y="120" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">90°</text><text x="359" y="164" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">m₁m₂ = −1</text></svg>
narration: The left-hand lines have the same gradient, so they are parallel. The right-hand pair meets at ninety degrees, so their finite gradients multiply to negative one. Handle horizontal and vertical lines separately: they form a perpendicular pair but a vertical line has no finite gradient.

formula: x-intercept: set y=0; y-intercept: set x=0.
condition: If both give the origin, choose a different second point.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A straight line meets the y-axis where x is zero and the x-axis where y is zero."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="38" y1="138" x2="444" y2="138" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="444.0,138.0 436.6,141.1 436.6,134.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="100" y1="158" x2="100" y2="22" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="100.0,22.0 103.1,29.4 96.9,29.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="452" y="146" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">x</text><text x="84" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">y</text><line x1="85" y1="20" x2="390" y2="153" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="100" cy="26.5" r="6" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="356" cy="138" r="6" fill="#3175ba" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="164" y="42" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">(0, b)</text><text x="360" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">(a, 0)</text><text x="286" y="75" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x = 0</text><text x="286" y="105" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">y = 0</text></svg>
narration: At the y-axis the x coordinate is zero. At the x-axis the y coordinate is zero. Substitute these values to get two points for drawing the line. If both calculations give the origin, find another point so that you have two distinct points to join.

task: Find the intersection of two lines
formula: Solve the two line equations simultaneously.
condition: Graph readings are approximate until confirmed algebraically.

Same y. Both equations.</text></svg>
narration: The crossing point has one x coordinate and one y coordinate that work in both equations. Solve the equations together to find the coordinates exactly. A graph helps predict the answer and spot mistakes, but use substitution into both equations to check an exact result.

task: Read a rate and sensible domain
formula: y=mx+c; m=Δy/Δx; c=value at x=0.
condition: State units and restrict the model to meaningful inputs.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A tank-volume graph begins at eighty litres and decreases at a constant rate until empty."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="135" x2="435" y2="135" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="435.0,135.0 427.6,138.1 427.6,131.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="151" x2="60" y2="20" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="60.0,20.0 63.1,27.4 56.9,27.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="40" x2="395" y2="135" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="60" cy="40" r="5" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="29" y="38" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">80</text><text x="204" y="66" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">−5 L/min</text><text x="443" y="165" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">t</text><text x="28" y="105" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">V</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Stop the model when V reaches 0</text></svg>
narration: The intercept is the starting amount and the slope is the amount gained or lost per input unit. This tank starts with eighty litres and loses five litres each minute. The line is useful only while the tank model makes sense; do not continue to negative volume.

task: Share a total or rebuild it from one share
formula: A:B=a:b ⇒ A=aN/(a+b), B=bN/(a+b). If A is known: one part=A/a; N=(a+b)A/a.
condition: N is the total. For reconstruction require a≠0.

narration: Each block represents one equal part. If you know the total, divide it by the total number of parts. If you know only A, divide that share by its own number of parts instead. Multiply the value of one part to find the other share or the whole.

formula: Ingredient amount=batch volume × ingredient parts/total parts.
condition: Find ingredient amounts before combining; do not average ratios.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two different-sized batches contain different proportions of juice, so their ingredient amounts must be calculated separately."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="40" y="25" width="120" height="110" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="40" y="91" width="120" height="44" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="300" y="25" width="140" height="110" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="300" y="102" width="140" height="33" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="100" y="58" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">1.5 L</text><text x="100" y="121" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">2/5 juice</text><text x="370" y="58" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">2 L</text><text x="370" y="126" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">3/10 juice</text><text x="240" y="84" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">+</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Add ingredient amounts, then form a ratio</text></svg>
narration: The green sections represent juice within two batches. Their fractions differ, and the batch volumes differ too. Multiply each batch volume by its juice fraction, then add juice amounts and water amounts separately. Use those combined amounts to form the final mixture ratio.

formula: Direct: y=kx. Inverse: xy=k. Equal workers × time=fixed work.
condition: Worker-time models assume equal productivity and divisible work.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Direct proportion preserves a ratio while inverse proportion preserves a product."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="25" y="25" width="200" height="105" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="255" y="25" width="200" height="105" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="125" y="57" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">Direct</text><line x1="70" y1="79" x2="175" y2="79" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="175.0,79.0 167.6,82.1 167.6,75.9" fill="#3175ba" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="125" y="116" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">y/x = k</text><text x="355" y="57" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">Inverse</text><line x1="300" y1="79" x2="350" y2="79" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="350.0,79.0 342.6,82.1 342.6,75.9" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="410" y1="96" x2="360" y2="96" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="360.0,96.0 367.4,92.9 367.4,99.1" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="355" y="126" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">xy = k</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Compare the constant relationship</text></svg>
narration: For direct proportion, increasing one quantity scales the other in the same direction and keeps their ratio constant. For inverse proportion, their product stays constant. More equally productive workers can reduce time for a fixed job, provided the work can be shared without a bottleneck.

task: Finish a job after the team changes
formula: Remaining worker-days=total worker-days−completed worker-days.
condition: Use the remaining work for the new team; then add elapsed time.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A completed portion is removed from a fixed total workload before the new team finishes the remainder."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="30" y="45" width="420" height="55" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="30" y="45" width="112" height="55" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="86" y="80" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">24</text><text x="295" y="80" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">66 remaining</text><text x="240" y="28" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">90 worker-days total</text><text x="240" y="144" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">66 ÷ 11 workers = 6 more days</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">4 elapsed + 6 more = 10 days</text></svg>
narration: The full bar is ninety worker-days of work. Six workers over four days complete twenty-four, leaving sixty-six. Divide only the remaining work by the new number of workers. Add the four days already spent when the question asks for the total project duration.

formula: 1 h=60 min; 1 day=24 h. Add 24 h to a next-day clock time before subtraction.
condition: Put both times on one continuous timeline.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A journey crosses midnight, splitting into eighteen minutes before midnight and seventy-seven after it."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="30" y1="70" x2="450" y2="70" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="450.0,70.0 442.6,73.1 442.6,66.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="70" y1="57" x2="70" y2="83" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="200" y1="57" x2="200" y2="83" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="400" y1="57" x2="400" y2="83" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="70" y="40" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">23:42</text><text x="200" y="40" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">00:00</text><text x="400" y="40" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">01:17</text><text x="135" y="114" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">18 min</text><text x="300" y="114" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">77 min</text><text x="240" y="163" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">18 + 77 = 95 minutes</text></svg>
narration: The clock resets at midnight but the journey does not. Split the duration into the part before midnight and the part after it, then add them. Alternatively treat the next-day finish as a time beyond twenty-four hours before subtracting the start time.

task: Choose the distance, speed or time formula
formula: v=d/t; d=vt; t=d/v; 1 m/s=3.6 km/h.
condition: Match time and distance units; 45 min=0.75 h.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A distance-speed-time triangle places distance above speed times time, with a unit conversion beneath."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="240,20 70,150 410,150" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="157" y1="84" x2="324" y2="84" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="240" y1="84" x2="240" y2="150" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="69" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">d</text><text x="186" y="130" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">v</text><text x="294" y="130" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">t</text><text x="70" y="49" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">distance</text><text x="408" y="49" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">÷ 3.6</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">m/s × 3.6 = km/h</text></svg>
narration: Read the triangle as distance equals speed times time. Divide distance by time to find speed, or distance by speed to find time. Convert minutes to hours when using kilometres per hour. Multiplying metres per second by three point six converts to kilometres per hour.

task: Find the average speed of a journey
formula: Average speed=total distance/total elapsed time.
condition: Include stops unless moving time is specifically requested.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two journey legs contribute separately to total distance and total time before division."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="55" x2="435" y2="55" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="435.0,55.0 427.6,58.1 427.6,51.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="138" y="39" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">48 km</text><text x="340" y="39" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">28 km</text><line x1="245" y1="44" x2="245" y2="66" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="138" y="90" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">40 min</text><text x="340" y="90" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">35 min</text><rect x="75" y="119" width="330" height="43" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="148" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">76 km ÷ 1.25 h = 60.8 km/h</text></svg>
narration: Calculate each leg distance using its own speed and duration. Add the distances and add the elapsed times, including stops when appropriate. Divide the totals. The average of two speed numbers is valid only in the special case where equal times were spent at those speeds.

formula: Each dot=one observation; labelled frequency-bar height=frequency.
condition: A high bar means a frequent category, not a larger data value.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A bar chart shows frequencies four, nine and seven for three categories."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="145" x2="430" y2="145" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="430.0,145.0 422.6,148.1 422.6,141.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="145" x2="45" y2="20" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="45.0,20.0 48.1,27.4 41.9,27.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="90" y="105" width="70" height="40" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="125" y="98" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">4</text><text x="125" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">A</text><rect x="205" y="55" width="70" height="90" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="48" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">9</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">B</text><rect x="320" y="75" width="70" height="70" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="355" y="68" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">7</text><text x="355" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">C</text><text x="114" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Frequency</text></svg>
narration: Read the labelled frequency scale before comparing the bar heights. The middle category occurs nine times, and the total is twenty. In a dot plot each dot represents one observation. Distinguish a category label from the number of observations recorded in that category.

task: Recover a missing value from a mean
formula: Mean=Σvalues/n; total=n×mean; missing=n×mean−known sum.
condition: Use the final number of values, including the missing one.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="The required total is split into the known sum and the missing value."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="30" y="40" width="300" height="58" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="330" y="40" width="120" height="58" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="180" y="77" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">known sum: 216</text><text x="390" y="77" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">?</text><text x="240" y="129" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">10 values × mean 25 = 250</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">missing = 250 − 216 = 34</text></svg>
narration: The full bar represents the total needed to produce the stated mean. Multiply the final number of values by that mean. Subtract the sum of all known values to find the gap. Here ten values averaging twenty-five need a total of two hundred and fifty.

task: Convert a pie angle to a share or total
condition: Use non-zero N; recovering N also requires θ≠0.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="An amber sector shows that a pie-chart angle represents the same fraction as part divided by whole."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="129" cy="88" r="67" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M129 88 L196 88 A67 67 0 0 0 149.7 24.3 Z" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="162" y="73" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">θ</text><text x="340" y="50" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">part f</text><line x1="277" y1="64" x2="403" y2="64" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="340" y="94" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">whole N</text><text x="340" y="135" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">= θ / 360°</text><text x="130" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Whole circle = 360°</text></svg>
narration: The sector fraction is its angle divided by three hundred and sixty degrees. That equals the category amount divided by the whole amount. Use the same proportion to find an angle, a category amount or an unknown total. An angle itself is not an amount of money.

formula: Density=f/w; frequency=bar area=density×class width.
condition: With unequal class widths, compare areas rather than heights.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two adjoining histogram bars have equal areas: the wider bar is half as high."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="145" x2="430" y2="145" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="430.0,145.0 422.6,148.1 422.6,141.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="145" x2="45" y2="20" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="45.0,20.0 48.1,27.4 41.9,27.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="80" y="35" width="100" height="110" rx="0" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="180" y="90" width="200" height="55" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="130" y="89" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">f</text><text x="280" y="128" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">same f</text><text x="130" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">w</text><text x="280" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">2w</text><text x="317" y="52" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">half the height</text></svg>
narration: Frequency is represented by bar area. The second bar is twice as wide but half as high, so both bars represent the same frequency. Divide a class frequency by its width to get density, then use density as the height when class widths differ.

formula: Median: position (n+1)/2 if n odd; average positions n/2 and n/2+1 if even. Mode=most frequent; range=max−min.
condition: Read the place-value key and put leaves in order.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="An ordered stem-and-leaf display has six values, so the median lies between the third and fourth observations."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="65" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">Stem</text><text x="246" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">Leaves</text><line x1="103" y1="38" x2="103" y2="119" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="65" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">1</text><text x="65" y="106" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">2</text><text x="240" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">2   8   8</text><text x="240" y="106" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">3   5   5</text><rect x="345" y="42" width="115" height="66" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="402" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">Key</text><text x="402" y="92" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">1|2=12</text><text x="240" y="154" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Middle values: 18 and 23</text></svg>
narration: The key tells you how to combine each stem with a leaf. Every leaf counts as one observation, including repeats. Order the leaves before finding the centre. With six observations, the middle values are eighteen and twenty-three, so their mean is the median.

condition: A smaller range indicates greater consistency by that measure only.
