narration: The dashed line marks the same median in both groups. The first group has a shorter distance from minimum to maximum, so its range is smaller. Describe centre and spread separately. A group can have greater consistency without having a higher typical result.

formula: Percentage change=(new−old)/old ×100%. A k-by-k pictogram has area factor k².
condition: Require old≠0. Check baselines, scales and pictogram areas.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Bars drawn from a baseline of ninety make a change from one hundred to one hundred and ten look doubled."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="55" y="85" width="80" height="60" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="170" y="25" width="80" height="120" rx="0" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="145" x2="267" y2="145" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="95" y="75" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">100</text><text x="210" y="22" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">110</text><text x="55" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="start" fill="#173349">axis starts at 90</text><text x="365" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Actual rise</text><text x="365" y="105" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">10%</text><text x="365" y="144" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">not 100%</text></svg>
narration: The right bar looks twice as tall because the axis starts at ninety. Compare the actual numbers: the rise is ten out of one hundred, or ten percent. Also inspect picture scaling; doubling both width and height makes a pictogram four times the area.

formula: aᵐaⁿ=aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ/aⁿ=aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ=aᵐⁿ; (ab)ⁿ=aⁿbⁿ; (a/b)ⁿ=aⁿ/bⁿ.
condition: Exclude zero in divisors/negative powers. Use positive bases for rational-index laws.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Three factors of x and two more factors combine into a product of five factors."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="29" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="29" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">x³ × x²</text><rect x="35" y="47" width="240" height="49" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="286" y="47" width="159" height="49" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="155" y="81" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">x × x × x</text><text x="365" y="81" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">x × x</text><line x1="35" y1="115" x2="445" y2="115" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="155" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">5 factors of x → x⁵</text></svg>
narration: A product joins the factors, so multiplying powers with the same base adds exponents. Division cancels matching factors, while a power of a power repeats the factors and multiplies exponents. Addition of separate powers follows neither rule. Check restrictions when dividing or using non-integer powers.

task: Interpret zero, negative and fractional powers
formula: a⁰=1; a⁻ⁿ=1/aⁿ; a^(m/n)=(ⁿ√a)ᵐ.
condition: For zero/negative powers a≠0. For the stated fractional rule, a>0 and n is a positive integer.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Three panels link zero powers to one, negative powers to reciprocals, and fractional powers to roots followed by powers."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="25" y="25" width="125" height="101" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="177" y="25" width="125" height="101" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="329" y="25" width="125" height="101" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="87" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="32" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">a⁰</text><text x="87" y="105" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">1</text><text x="239" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="32" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">a⁻ⁿ</text><text x="239" y="105" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">1/aⁿ</text><text x="391" y="65" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">a^(m/n)</text><text x="391" y="105" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">root → power</text><text x="240" y="166" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Denominator: root. Numerator: power.</text></svg>
narration: A zero exponent gives one for a non-zero base. A negative exponent tells you to take a reciprocal. In a fractional exponent, the denominator names the root and the numerator gives the power. For this rule use a positive base and a positive integer root index.

task: Solve an equation with equal bases
formula: For b>0, b≠1: bᵘ=bᵛ ⇒ u=v.
condition: Changing 27 to 3³ multiplies the whole outer exponent by 3.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Rewriting twenty-seven as three cubed puts both sides on a common base before equating exponents."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="34" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">3^(2x−1) = 27^(x−2)</text><text x="240" y="79" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">3^(2x−1) = 3^[3(x−2)]</text><line x1="40" y1="97" x2="440" y2="97" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="135" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">2x − 1 = 3(x − 2)</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Same base → match exponents</text></svg>
narration: First rewrite both sides as powers of the same suitable base. Twenty-seven becomes three cubed, so the entire exponent x minus two must be multiplied by three. Then equate the exponents and solve the resulting equation. The base must be positive and different from one.

formula: √(ab)=√a√b; p√q+r√q=(p+r)√q.
condition: Use a,b≥0. Combine only matching simplified square-root parts.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Seventy-two splits into the square factor thirty-six and the remaining factor two."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="30" y="35" width="180" height="60" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="120" y="75" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="32" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">√72</text><line x1="220" y1="65" x2="260" y2="65" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="260.0,65.0 252.6,68.1 252.6,61.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="270" y="35" width="180" height="60" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="360" y="75" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">√36 × √2</text><text x="240" y="141" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="33" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">6√2</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Take out the largest square factor</text></svg>
narration: Look inside the root for a square factor. Seventy-two is thirty-six times two, so its square root is six root two. Simplify all surds before deciding which can combine. Add coefficients only when their remaining square-root parts match; do not add different radicands.

task: Multiply surds or clear a root denominator
condition: a,b≥0 for products; b>0 for quotients; q>0 for rationalising.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Multiplying both parts of three over root two by root two clears the irrational denominator without changing the value."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="83" y="67" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">3</text><line x1="46" y1="78" x2="120" y2="78" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="83" y="112" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">√2</text><text x="158" y="89" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">×</text><text x="235" y="67" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">√2</text><line x1="199" y1="78" x2="271" y2="78" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="235" y="112" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">√2</text><text x="307" y="89" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">=</text><text x="387" y="67" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">3√2</text><line x1="343" y1="78" x2="431" y2="78" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="387" y="112" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">2</text><text x="240" y="167" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Multiply numerator AND denominator</text></svg>
narration: Multiply the fraction by root two over root two, which equals one. The denominator becomes two and the value stays unchanged. Changing only the denominator would change the fraction. When squaring a sum or difference of surds, include the middle product as well as the two squares.

formula: Product=ab×10ᵐ⁺ⁿ; quotient=(a/b)×10ᵐ⁻ⁿ, b≠0.
condition: Normalise a non-zero answer so 1≤|coefficient|<10.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="The coefficient calculation is separated from the power-of-ten calculation before the answer is normalised."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="28" y="27" width="200" height="52" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="250" y="27" width="200" height="52" rx="7" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><text x="128" y="62" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">(6.4 ÷ 2.5)</text><text x="350" y="62" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">10^(9 − 6)</text><text x="240" y="64" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">×</text><line x1="240" y1="87" x2="240" y2="109" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><polygon points="240.0,109.0 236.9,101.6 243.1,101.6" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><text x="240" y="140" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="32" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">2.56 × 10³</text><text x="240" y="172" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">1 ≤ |coefficient| < 10</text></svg>
narration: Work on the coefficients and powers of ten separately. For division, divide coefficients and subtract exponents. For multiplication, multiply coefficients and add exponents. Combine the two results, then move the decimal point if needed so the non-zero answer is written in normalised standard form.

formula: Write a common power of ten; then add or subtract coefficients.
condition: Do not add or subtract exponents for addition or subtraction.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="One term is rewritten so both quantities use ten to the ninth power before their coefficients are subtracted."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="31" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">6.4 × 10⁹ − 7.5 × 10⁸</text><rect x="28" y="51" width="424" height="48" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="83" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">6.4 × 10⁹ − 0.75 × 10⁹</text><text x="240" y="140" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">(6.4 − 0.75) × 10⁹</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Match powers before adding coefficients</text></svg>
narration: The terms must be expressed using the same power of ten before their coefficients can combine. Rewrite seven point five times ten to the eighth as zero point seven five times ten to the ninth. Then subtract coefficients while keeping that common power unchanged.

formula: Decimal places count from the decimal point; significant figures start at the first non-zero digit.
condition: Use the next digit to decide rounding; retain place value.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Leading zeros are separated from the first two significant digits; the next digit tells whether to round up."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><text x="85" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">0.00</text><text x="179" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">6</text><rect x="204" y="25" width="44" height="46" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><text x="226" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">2</text><text x="302" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">84</text><text x="102" y="104" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">leading zeros</text><text x="235" y="104" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">keep 2 digits</text><text x="382" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">→</text><text x="382" y="104" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">8 rounds up</text><text x="240" y="164" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">0.006284 → 0.0063 (2 s.f.)</text></svg>
narration: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit, so the zeros before six do not count. Keep the requested number of digits, then inspect the next one. In this example eight rounds the two up to three. Decimal places instead count positions after the decimal point.

task: Enter brackets and test a claim
formula: Bracket compound numerators, denominators and radicands. One valid counterexample disproves a universal claim.
condition: One agreeing example cannot prove an identity for all values.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Squaring a bracket gives forty-nine while adding separate squares gives twenty-five, disproving an incorrect identity."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="25" y="28" width="200" height="104" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="255" y="28" width="200" height="104" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="125" y="59" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">(3 + 4)²</text><text x="125" y="107" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">49</text><text x="355" y="59" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">3² + 4²</text><text x="355" y="107" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">25</text><text x="240" y="84" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">≠</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">One counterexample disproves “always”</text></svg>
narration: Brackets tell the calculator which operation belongs together. Compare squaring the whole sum with adding the two separate squares. Three and four produce different answers, so they disprove the claim that the expressions are always equal. A single agreeing example would not prove a universal identity.

formula: uv=0 ⇒ u=0 or v=0.
condition: First rearrange the equation so the product equals zero.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A zero product splits into two possible zero factors and therefore two candidate roots."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="31" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">x² − x − 12 = 0</text><text x="240" y="76" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">(x − 4)(x + 3) = 0</text><line x1="181" y1="88" x2="115" y2="115" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="115.0,115.0 120.6,109.3 123.0,115.1" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="299" y1="88" x2="365" y2="115" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="365.0,115.0 357.0,115.1 359.4,109.3" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="35" y="122" width="170" height="43" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="275" y="122" width="170" height="43" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="120" y="152" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">x = 4</text><text x="360" y="152" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x = −3</text></svg>
narration: Move all terms to one side so the equation equals zero. Factorise that expression. A product can equal zero only if at least one factor is zero, so solve each factor equation separately. This zero-product rule does not apply when the product equals a non-zero number.

condition: Write ax²+bx+c=0 first; keep the signs of a, b and c.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A quadratic in standard form identifies all three coefficients including their signs."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="48" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="54" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">3x² − 5x − 2 = 0</text><text x="87" y="109" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">a = 3</text><text x="240" y="109" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">b = −5</text><text x="391" y="109" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">c = −2</text><text x="240" y="164" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Keep the sign with each coefficient</text></svg>
narration: Write the equation in standard form and identify a, b and c with their signs. Substitute them into the quadratic formula using brackets around negative values. The plus or minus produces two possibilities. The entire numerator must be divided by two a, and a must be non-zero.

task: Predict how many real roots exist
formula: D=b²−4ac: D>0 → two; D=0 → repeated; D<0 → no real roots.
condition: A negative D means no real roots, not two negative roots.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Three parabolas cross, touch or miss the horizontal axis, matching the three discriminant cases."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="33" y1="103" x2="155" y2="103" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M39 30 Q95 210 151 30" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><text x="95" y="145" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">D > 0</text><text x="95" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">2 roots</text><line x1="188" y1="103" x2="310" y2="103" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M194 30 Q250 176 306 30" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><text x="250" y="145" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">D = 0</text><text x="250" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">1 repeated</text><line x1="343" y1="103" x2="465" y2="103" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M349 30 Q405 120 461 30" fill="none" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="3"/><text x="405" y="145" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">D < 0</text><text x="405" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">0 real roots</text></svg>
narration: The discriminant tells you how many real roots the quadratic formula can produce. Positive means two distinct crossings, zero means one repeated root where the curve touches the axis, and negative means no real crossing. This counts real solutions; it does not tell whether individual roots are positive or negative.

formula: Outer area=(L+2x)(W+2x); border area=outer area−LW.
condition: A border on both sides adds 2x to each dimension.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A uniform border surrounds all four sides of an inner rectangle."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="80" y="25" width="320" height="125" rx="0" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="122" y="57" width="236" height="62" rx="0" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="96" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="29" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">L × W</text><text x="240" y="47" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x</text><text x="103" y="94" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x</text><text x="378" y="94" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x</text><text x="240" y="145" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Outer: (L+2x) by (W+2x)</text></svg>
narration: The amber border has width x everywhere. It adds x at each end of each dimension, giving length L plus two x and width W plus two x. Multiply for the outer area. Subtract the inner area only when the question gives or asks for the border area.

task: Build and check a quadratic model
formula: Translate the original relation → solve → apply the domain.
condition: Reject a root only when it violates a stated or physical restriction.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A rectangle has width x, length x plus three and area forty, creating a quadratic equation."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="74" y="35" width="260" height="94" rx="0" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="204" y="90" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="29" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">Area 40</text><text x="204" y="25" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">x + 3</text><text x="363" y="87" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">x</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">x(x+3)=40 → x>0</text></svg>
narration: Start from the relationship in the story. This rectangle has area equal to width times length, so x times x plus three equals forty. Solve the resulting quadratic, then check both roots against the model. A negative width is rejected because a physical length must be positive.

task: Find both times a target is reached
formula: Set model expression=target, then rearrange to zero and solve.
condition: Both roots may be valid; test them against the model’s domain.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A horizontal target line crosses a quadratic model twice."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="141" x2="435" y2="141" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="435.0,141.0 427.6,144.1 427.6,137.9" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="45" y1="155" x2="45" y2="22" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="45.0,22.0 48.1,29.4 41.9,29.4" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M60 145 Q240 -65 420 145" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="45" y1="90" x2="430" y2="90" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><circle cx="115" cy="90" r="5" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="365" cy="90" r="5" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><text x="93" y="120" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">n₁</text><text x="386" y="120" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">n₂</text><text x="349" y="58" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">target</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">Solve P(n) = target</text></svg>
narration: The target is a horizontal level, and the curve can meet it on the way up and again on the way down. Set the model equal to that target before rearranging to zero. Solve for both inputs and retain every answer allowed by the situation and domain.

task: Build an equation from its roots
formula: Roots r,s: a(x−r)(x−s)=0; expand to ax²−a(r+s)x+ars=0, a≠0.
condition: A negative root creates a plus sign in its factor.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two specified roots are converted into zero factors, with a non-zero scale controlling the leading coefficient."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="25" y="25" width="160" height="53" rx="7" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="295" y="25" width="160" height="53" rx="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="none" stroke-width="2" /><text x="105" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">root −3</text><text x="375" y="60" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">root 4</text><line x1="105" y1="84" x2="159" y2="114" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><polygon points="159.0,114.0 151.0,113.1 154.1,107.7" fill="#3175ba" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="375" y1="84" x2="321" y2="114" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2" /><polygon points="321.0,114.0 325.9,107.7 329.0,113.1" fill="#b96a12" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2" /><text x="240" y="140" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="29" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">a(x+3)(x−4)=0</text><text x="240" y="172" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">a ≠ 0</text></svg>
narration: A root r means x minus r must be one factor. Negative three therefore gives x plus three, while four gives x minus four. Multiply these factors, and use a non-zero multiplier if a leading coefficient is specified. Taking a equal to one gives the monic equation.

formula: AA: two equal angle pairs suffice. ΔABC∼ΔDEF ⇒ AB/DE=BC/EF=AC/DF.
condition: Corresponding angles are equal; all matching lengths use one scale.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two differently sized triangles use ordered vertex labels to identify corresponding sides."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="35,137 185,137 135,42" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="263,137 448,137 386,20" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="25" y="166" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">A</text><text x="190" y="166" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">B</text><text x="135" y="32" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">C</text><text x="260" y="166" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">D</text><text x="453" y="166" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">E</text><text x="413" y="25" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">F</text><path d="M55 137 A20 20 0 0 1 48 120" fill="none" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M283 137 A20 20 0 0 1 276 120" fill="none" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/></svg>
narration: First establish two matching angle pairs. Use the order of the named vertices to match corresponding sides: A with D, B with E and C with F. Form ratios using the same triangle order each time. Similar shapes can be rotated or reversed, so apparent position is not enough.

task: Use a parallel cut in a triangle
formula: DE∥BC ⇒ AD/AB=AE/AC=DE/BC; AD/DB=AE/EC.
condition: Match whole with whole or remaining part with remaining part; denominators ≠0.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A line parallel to the base cuts off a smaller triangle with matching angles."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="240,28 65,143 415,143" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="161" y1="80" x2="319" y2="80" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><text x="265" y="27" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">A</text><text x="46" y="163" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">B</text><text x="434" y="163" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">C</text><text x="140" y="75" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">D</text><text x="340" y="75" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">E</text><text x="240" y="119" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">DE ∥ BC</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">small side / whole side</text></svg>
narration: The green cut is parallel to the base, so the small top triangle is similar to the whole triangle. Ratios of corresponding full sides match. If you compare the top part with the leftover part on one side, use the same type of comparison on the other side.

formula: Vertically opposite angles + a parallel-line angle pair ⇒ AA similarity.
condition: Match vertices before taking ratios, even when a triangle is reversed.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Two triangles form a bow-tie shape with equal vertically opposite angles and parallel outside sides."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="65,37 65,143 240,90" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="240,90 420,35.5 420,144.5" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="42" y="35" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">A</text><text x="42" y="164" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">B</text><text x="443" y="30" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">C</text><text x="443" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">D</text><text x="240" y="74" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">O</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">AB ∥ CD</text></svg>
narration: The angles at O are vertically opposite and therefore equal. The parallel outer sides create a second equal angle pair, proving similarity by AA. Follow the matching vertices through the crossing rather than matching left with left. Then use consistent corresponding-side ratios to find an unknown length.

task: Use shadows and a right triangle
formula: h₁/s₁=h₂/s₂; c²=a²+b²; c=√(a²+b²); a=√(c²−b²).
condition: Shadow ratios assume parallel sun rays on level ground; c is the hypotenuse.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A small pole and a taller object form similar shadow triangles; the slant is a hypotenuse."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="46,136 46,84 108,136" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="197,136 197,31 322,136" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="23" y="110" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">h₁</text><text x="77" y="165" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">s₁</text><text x="177" y="86" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">h₂</text><text x="265" y="165" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">s₂</text><text x="286" y="67" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">c</text><line x1="197" y1="31" x2="322" y2="136" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="3"/><text x="367" y="104" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">parallel</text><text x="367" y="130" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">rays</text></svg>
narration: Parallel sunlight creates matching angles, and level ground makes both triangles right-angled. Their height-to-shadow ratios are equal. After finding the height, use Pythagoras if the question asks for the slant distance. Keep perpendicular height, horizontal shadow and diagonal distance clearly distinguished.

formula: Same arc: centre=2×edge. Same segment: edge angles equal. Diameter: edge=90°. Cyclic opposite angles sum to 180°.
condition: Identify the same arc; the relevant centre angle may be reflex.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Centre and circumference angles stand on the same chord and arc, alongside diameter and cyclic-angle reminders."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="120" cy="86" r="66" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="65" y1="122" x2="120" y2="86" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="175" y1="122" x2="120" y2="86" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="65" y1="122" x2="145" y2="25" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="175" y1="122" x2="145" y2="25" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="120" cy="86" r="4" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><text x="120" y="117" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">2θ</text><text x="144" y="66" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">θ</text><text x="341" y="53" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">Same arc: 2θ</text><text x="341" y="93" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">Diameter: 90°</text><text x="341" y="133" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">Cyclic: α+β=180°</text></svg>
narration: Identify the chord endpoints and the arc each angle stands on before choosing a theorem. A central angle on the same arc doubles the circumference angle. Other useful cases are a right angle on a diameter, equal angles in the same segment, and supplementary opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral.

formula: α+β+γ=180° in a Euclidean triangle.
condition: Use an auxiliary parallel line and known angle facts, not the theorem being proved.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A parallel through a triangle’s top vertex relocates the two base angles beside the top angle on a straight line."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="240,48 95,145 385,145" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="40" y1="48" x2="440" y2="48" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="121" y="137" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">α</text><text x="358" y="137" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">β</text><text x="240" y="85" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">γ</text><text x="190" y="73" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">α</text><text x="291" y="73" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">β</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">α + γ + β = 180°</text></svg>
narration: Draw a line through the top vertex parallel to the base. Alternate-angle facts move copies of the two base angles next to the top angle. The three angles now lie on one straight line, whose angle is one hundred and eighty degrees. That establishes the triangle-angle sum.

formula: Exterior angle θ=α+β, the two non-adjacent interior angles.
condition: Do not include the adjacent interior angle in the remote-angle sum.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="A triangle side is extended so an exterior angle is adjacent to the third interior angle."><rect x="0" y="0" width="480" height="180" rx="0" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="215,30 80,135 350,135" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="350" y1="135" x2="450" y2="135" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="113" y="125" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#087f75">α</text><text x="215" y="70" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#3175ba">β</text><text x="321" y="124" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" text-anchor="middle" fill="#173349">γ</text><text x="379" y="116" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">θ</text><text x="240" y="169" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="29" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b96a12">θ = α + β</text></svg>
narration: The exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle make a straight angle. The three interior angles also add to a straight angle. Subtract the shared adjacent angle from both equal totals. What remains is the exterior angle equal to the sum of the two remote interior angles.

formula: AB∥CD and BC∥AD; diagonal AC gives ΔABC≅ΔCDA by ASA.
condition: A parallelogram diagonal need not bisect each corner angle.

narration: Draw diagonal AC. Each pair of parallel opposite sides gives a pair of equal alternate angles. The diagonal is a side common to both triangles. Angle-side-angle congruence then matches the remaining sides and angles, proving the opposite parts of the parallelogram are equal.

formula: AB²+AC²=BC²; BC is the hypotenuse.
condition: Drop AD perpendicular to BC; D need not be its midpoint.

narration: Drop a perpendicular from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse. The two smaller triangles are similar to the original triangle. Their side ratios give AB squared equal to BC times BD and AC squared equal to BC times DC. Add, using BD plus DC equal to BC.

formula: Central angle on the same arc = 2∠ACB.
condition: Keep the chosen arc fixed; some cases use a reflex central angle.

narration: Join the centre to the three circumference points. Equal radii create isosceles triangles, so their base angles match. Use triangle-angle or exterior-angle reasoning on the two parts and combine them. Keep the same arc throughout; the central angle required by the theorem can be reflex.

task: Use equal sides and angle structure
formula: Isosceles: equal sides ⇒ equal opposite angles. Equilateral: all sides equal, angles 60°. Parallelogram: opposite parts equal, adjacent angles sum to 180°.
condition: Equal adjacent parallelogram sides alone do not make equilateral triangles.

narration: In an isosceles triangle, look opposite the equal sides to find equal angles. An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal and all angles sixty degrees. In a parallelogram, opposite parts match while neighbouring angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees. Apply the correct structure to the named shape.
